name: Hopi (Hopituh Shi-nu-mu)
notes: A Puebloan people of northeastern Arizona, Uto-Aztecan-language (distinct from most Rio Grande Pueblo languages: Tanoan and Keresan) — genuinely distinct from "Pueblo" generally, not a synonym for it. Continuous occupation of the Hopi mesas since roughly 1100–1150 CE (Old Oraibi); the popular "oldest continuously inhabited settlement in the US" superlative is a contested tourism claim with a real competing claimant, Acoma Pueblo, and no precise scholarly dendrochronological founding date exists for Oraibi — report as contested, not settled (see claim_old_oraibi_dating_contested). Descended from/continuous with the Ancestral Puebloan archaeological tradition; "Anasazi" (Navajo-derived, glossed "ancient enemies") is explicitly rejected by named Hopi cultural authorities as derogatory (see claim_anasazi_terminology_rejected) in favor of "Ancestral Puebloan" or the Hopi-specific "Hisatsinom."
